_readme: Home's type roles, one row per element, keyed by the literal string BOTH
and the two sources, and fails if either platform's call site has moved off
the value here. Two reviews each listed a different set of 'N type roles
disagree between platforms'; hand-reconciling a number in two languages is
not a fix, because nothing stops the next edit moving one side. This table
is the thing that stops it.
size is the point size at the DEFAULT font scale (the compact/narrow-screen
branches are call-site fallbacks and are not gated). weight is the shared
name: Android's FontWeight.SemiBold and SwiftUI's .semibold are both
What is NOT here: the greeting only. Android renders `greeting + ","` and
iOS interpolates `\(greetingWord)`, so neither side has a literal; the lint
prints that one gap on every run. The suggestions row and the Video chip USED
to be in this list because their copy arrives as a parameter — the lint now
into the Text() that renders the parameter, which is how the chip's 10.5 vs 13
disagreement was found after two reviews had listed it and no check had seen
